thread.title: Apple Music Passes 40 Million Subscribers, Spooking Spotify Investors

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Music Passes 40 Million Subscribers, Spooking Spotify Investors
text:
Apple 's ( AAPL ) subscription music service Apple Music has passed 40 million paying subscribers, according to a news report, which sent shares of recent IPO Spotify Technology ( SPOT ) tumbling on Wednesday.
X The company disclosed the news in an internal memo announcing new leadership for the business, according to Variety .
It also has promoted Oliver Schusser to head Apple Music Worldwide. He will serve as vice president of Apple Music and international content and report to the corporation's services chief Eddy Cue, Variety said.
Schusser previously led efforts outside the U.S. related to the App Store, iTunes portals for movies and TV shows, iBooks and Apple Podcasts. He also played a key role in Apple's acquisition of music discovery service Shazam.

Please contact customer service CLOSE In addition to more than 40 million paying subscribers, Apple Music has 8 million users on free trial plans, Variety said. Apple offers the service in 115 countries.
Streaming music leader Spotify, based in Stockholm, Sweden, has 71 million paying subscribers worldwide.
Spotify went public on April 3, starting at 165.90 and hitting a high of 169. It dropped 3.4% to close at 149.57 on the stock market today .
Apple shares slipped 0.5% to finish at 172.44.
Apple Stock Initiated With Buy Rating Meanwhile, Monness Crespi Hardt analyst Brian White initiated coverage on Apple with a buy rating and price target of 235. White previously covered Apple at Drexel Hamilton.
"We view Apple as one of the most underappreciated stocks in the world with a valuation that remains depressed and our expectation that the company is poised to cross the $1 trillion market capitalization milestone over the next 12 months," White said in a note to clients. "In the near term, we believe there are attractive capital return opportunities to be unveiled and we look forward to another round of iPhone innovations in September."
Apple's iPhone X kicked off a "durable cycle" for iPhone sales, rather than a "supercycle," as some had predicted, White said. Apple introduced the iPhone X along with the iPhone 8 series handsets at an event last fall.
